items.title: 3 things to never do with a credit card
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Learn how to spot the 3 most common traps of credit cards, and how they can lock you into a cycle of interest, fees, and debt.

--

While useful for secure purchasing, emergencies, and building credit scores, credit cards can make it difficult to avoid overspending. And this is no accident. Credit card systems are intentionally designed to encourage spending and lock you into a cycle of interest and fees. So, how can you avoid their most common traps? Explore 3 ways that credit card companies take advantage of their customers.

Directed by Jeff Le Bars, JetPropulsion.space.

items.title: Which is better: Buying or renting a home? - Ella Feldman
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Dig into the dilemma of whether it's financially better to rent or buy a home, and explore the pros and cons of each choice.

--

Nobody was surprised when Morgan and her twin sister Lisa moved into identical houses right next to each other. The only difference? Morgan bought her house, while Lisa is renting hers. For generations, conventional wisdom has been that homeownership is financially better than renting. But is this actually true? Ella Feldman follows the twins in their housing journey to see who comes out on top.

Lesson by Ella Feldman, directed by Josh Pilch, Augenblick Studios.

items.title: Why is Queen Victoria so controversial? - Carolyn Harris
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Queen Victoria presided over a golden age of the British Empire — but was she its moral compass or obsessed with her reputation?

--

During her 63-year reign, Queen Victoria was a model of morality and restraint. So much so that the 19th century is called the “Victorian Age” and is still associated with these qualities. But was she the empire’s moral compass during a time of dizzying change, or an imperialist monarch who cared more about her reputation than her subjects? Carolyn Harris puts this controversial figure on trial.

Lesson by Carolyn Harris, directed by Igor Ćorić, Artrake Studio.

items.title: Why are AI data centers using so much electricity? - Sajan Saini
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore the challenges and possibilities of AI data centers, and how these rapidly expanding complexes use energy and resources.

--

Since 2019, over a thousand warehouse campuses have popped up around the world. Each complex covers nearly 100,000 square meters, uses as much water as a small town, and as much electricity as a small city. These are AI data centers — facilities for running and training Large Language Models like ChatGPT. Sajan Saini explores the challenges and possibilities of these rapidly expanding complexes.

Lesson by Sajan Saini, directed by Vicente Numpaque, Dr3i Studio.

items.title: Do we actually know how magnets work? - Rachel Yang
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore the physics of magnetism, and how its properties are used in modern technologies like MRI machines, hard drives, and more.

--

In the 1920s, physicists still had many unanswered questions about magnetism. While they knew that every electron and proton have invisible, magnetic fields that radiate out in closed loops from one end to the other, they wondered: what determines the direction of these magnetic fields? And if every atom is composed of these tiny magnets, why isn’t everything magnetic? Rachel Yang investigates.

Lesson by Rachel Yang, directed by Tolga Yıldız, Kozmonot Animation Studio.

This video was made possible in collaboration with Nobel Prize Outreach, and with support from the Sloan Foundation

items.title: 4 ways to fix your attention span - Shannon Odell
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore 4 strategies to build a better attention span, manage distractions, and help your brain stay focused on its tasks.

--

Check out our 500-piece jigsaw puzzle, created in partnership with Ravensburger and featuring art from this very TED-Ed animation: http://t.ted.com/3kB0raN 

In today’s world, our attention is being pulled in more directions than ever before. This can make finding focus— for work, school, and even the things we love— feel almost impossible. So, how can you improve and better protect your attention span? Shannon Odell shares strategies on how to manage distractions and give your brain the best chance at focusing.

Lesson by Shannon Odell, directed by Héloïse Dorsan-Rachet.
